title: Elevated CK / suspected myopathy
consultQuestion: High CK with proximal weakness — statin myopathy, myositis, or something else?
keyHistory: Tempo: rapid (IMNM, antisynthetase) vs slow over years (IBM, dystrophy)
Statin exposure, including past exposure — HMGCR myopathy can persist or worsen after stopping
Rash (heliotrope, Gottron, shawl), mechanic's hands, Raynaud, arthritis, dyspnea/cough (ILD)
Cancer history or symptoms; checkpoint inhibitors
keyExam: Pattern: proximal symmetric (IMNM, DM, antisynthetase) vs quadriceps + finger flexors, often asymmetric (IBM)
Neck flexor and bulbar weakness, respiratory muscle weakness
redFlags: Myocarditis signs (troponin, arrhythmia) — especially with checkpoint inhibitors

clues: Rapid proximal, lumbopelvic weakness, very high CK; statin exposure (HMGCR)
Typical rash; cancer risk high with TIF-1γ, NXP2
Myositis, arthritis, ILD, mechanic's hands; anti-Jo-1 and others
Slow, quadriceps and finger flexors, dysphagia; CK normal to moderate

differential.dx: Checkpoint inhibitor myositis (± myocarditis, MG overlap)
Genetic myopathy (especially age <30), hypothyroid myopathy, rhabdomyolysis

workup.test: CK, aldolase, LFTs (AST/ALT may be muscle), TSH, BMP
notes: Acute muscle injury: AST/ALT ratio >3, falling toward ~1 within days because AST clears faster; ratio ~1.2 in polymyositis (Nathwani 2005)
GGT confirms a hepatic source of alkaline phosphatase — it doesn't localize AST/ALT, and phenytoin and barbiturates raise it (ACG 2017)

indication: High CK, especially with checkpoint inhibitors

workup.test: Myositis-specific antibodies including anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP
notes: Commercial line-blots don't cover all antibodies; methods differ (ENMC 2017)

indication: Choose biopsy site; distinguish edema from fatty replacement

notes: Not mandatory with a well-defined clinical–serologic picture; essential if seronegative and for all IBM (NEJM 2026)

indication: Dermatomyositis, HMGCR-positive, seronegative IMNM, age >40, dysphagia

decisionRules.recommendation: Anti-HMGCR myopathy (biopsy, EMG, MRI not required for subtyping); stop statin

decisionRules.condition: Elevated CK + proximal weakness, no myositis-specific antibody, biopsy with scattered necrotic fibers, necrosis/regeneration at different stages, macrophage-predominant sparse infiltrates

decisionRules.recommendation: Test anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP so a treatable myopathy isn't missed

initialSteps: IMNM treatment (steroids plus early second agent; IVIG for HMGCR, rituximab for SRP): see ENMC 2017 — rheumatology/neuromuscular co-management
recsTemplate: Myositis panel including HMGCR and SRP antibodies
EMG; muscle MRI to guide biopsy
Muscle biopsy [if seronegative or IBM suspected]
disposition: Inpatient if dysphagia, respiratory weakness, myocarditis, or rhabdomyolysis
institutionVaries: Myositis panel send-out lab and turnaround
Muscle biopsy processing (needs a neuromuscular pathology lab)
pearls: Cancer occurs in about 10% of adults with myositis within 3 years of diagnosis; risk is high with seronegative IMNM, TIF-1γ, NXP2, anti-OJ, and seronegative DM over age 40; intermediate with HMGCR, Mi-2, MDA5, SAE (NEJM 2026 Table 1)
IBM: quadriceps and finger flexor weakness is almost pathognomonic; CK normal to moderately raised (NEJM 2026)
Under age 30, distinguish early IMNM from genetic myopathy — antibody status matters most (NEJM 2026)
Statin-associated HMGCR myopathy persists or worsens after the statin is stopped (ENMC 2017)
Raised ALT doesn't prove liver injury — ALT rises substantially with muscle necrosis; muscle disease raises AST/ALT with AST predominance early; screen with CK ± aldolase (Nathwani 2005; ACG 2017)
